en.title: Elder Scrolls 6 Lead Designer Reveals Todd Howard's Starfield Detour
en.summary: A former lead designer for **The Elder Scrolls** series has shed light on why **The Elder Scrolls 6** was delayed and how **Todd Howard**'s passion project, **Starfield**, altered Bethesda's development path. The revelations come from **Kurt Kuhlmann**, who spent over two decades at the studio.
en.body:
The long-awaited **The Elder Scrolls 6** has been a source of endless speculation for years, but a former insider has offered a candid explanation for the extended development cycle. **Kurt Kuhlmann**, who served as a lead designer on **Skyrim** and spent more than two decades at **Bethesda Game Studios**, revealed that the traditional alternating development of **Fallout** and **The Elder Scrolls** was disrupted by **Todd Howard**'s personal vision for a new space-faring RPG.

Kuhlmann, who departed Bethesda in 2023, suggested that the studio's focus shifted dramatically towards **Starfield**, effectively sidelining the next mainline **Elder Scrolls** title. He indicated that the decision to pursue **Starfield** wasn't a collective studio initiative, but rather a directive from **Howard**. This pivot meant that **The Elder Scrolls 6** was pushed back, with Kuhlmann himself reportedly being promised the lead role on the project, only to see that promise superseded by the demands of **Starfield** and the subsequent development of **Fallout 76**.

## The Fallout Fanatic's Dilemma

The intense dedication of **Fallout: New Vegas** fans, often vocal about their preferences and critiques of **Bethesda**'s output, has not gone unnoticed by the developers. Kuhlmann’s insights touch upon the studio's awareness of this passionate, sometimes demanding, fanbase. While **Bethesda** developers generally express pride in their work and respect for peers like **Obsidian Entertainment** (the creators of **New Vegas**), the persistent online discourse and criticism, particularly from content creators, can be grating.

It's understandable why **Todd Howard** might be protective of the **Elder Scrolls** franchise, aiming to avoid a situation where a particular fan interpretation or demand dictates the creative direction. The situation with **Fallout: New Vegas** fans, while a testament to the game's enduring quality, also highlights the challenges of managing community expectations, especially when those expectations clash with a studio's evolving vision. This delicate balance seems to influence decisions about mainline spinoffs and the overall direction of the studio's flagship titles.

## What's Next

While details about **The Elder Scrolls 6** remain scarce, the insights from **Kurt Kuhlmann** underscore the significant shifts within **Bethesda Game Studios**' development priorities. The focus has clearly been on launching and supporting **Starfield** and **Fallout 76**, with **The Elder Scrolls 6** now the primary long-term project. Fans will be eagerly awaiting further official updates on the game's progress, with no concrete release window announced yet.

content_raw: I want to establish my old school RPG sicko bona fides really quick: My favorite Fallout games are 1 and New Vegas. My least favorite is 3 (4 is better than it gets credit for in critical circles). I really did not like Starfield and did not make it past the first planet. Obsidian is one of my favorites to ever do it. Troika Games forever. With that out of the way, it is deranged how a lot of fans talk online about Bethesda as a studio, and Todd Howard as a guy. I have no doubt as to the accuracy of Kuhlmann's assessment of his former boss. And I don't blame Howard one bit for being protective of the series in this way⁠. It's pretty relatable, and I'm sure it wasn't the only consideration around avoiding mainline-style spinoffs, as Kuhlmann's thoughts on ESO indicate. Reading this in bad faith, you could parse it as an admission of weakness or insecurity, but I don't see it that way. I've spoken to senior Bethesda devs myself and watched them in other interviews: They're proud of their own work, speak positively of New Vegas, and seem to respect their peers at Obsidian. I think it's YouTubers impugning their character or calling for their coworkers to be fired over a perceived mishandling of the series that gets on their nerves. Fallout memers seem to have gotten what they wanted, but in a monkey's paw kind of way. Obsidian is making a new Fallout game now, but with a gun to its head.
